text:
alex.w: paging: oncall triggered for possible privacy exposure from upload service. seeing anomalous 500s and a partial S3 presign leak to a debug bucket. can oncall confirm scope? :rotating_light:
oncall-bot: PagerDuty alert routed to alex.w and samir.p — Incident 2026-1849997777. Acknowledge within 5m to avoid escalation.
mira.k: oncall, I can join — I was just investigating elevated errors from the upload worker. small chance of presign URLs logged to stdout for 12 minutes.
samir.p: acked. grabbing logs now. can we stop new presigns ASAP?
alex.w: yes — executing temporary config flip: `UPLOAD_PRESIGN_ENABLED=false` on canary. Mira, please watch queue depth.
ops-runner: deploybot: rolled config toggle to canary (service/upload/replica-2). no errors on canary after 30s.
security-guy: quick question — are these presigns time-limited? TTL was 24h last I checked. If leaked, public access window could be long.
mira.k: TTL = 24h by default. some customers use shorter, but cannot assume.
eng-lead: we need immediate customer-scope decision. Is this internal debug only or could it include customer object keys?
samir.p: early log parsing shows about 120 unique keys. ~70% look like internal test prefixes, ~30% look like customer uploads (hashed prefixes).
alex.w: ok that suggests potential customer-exposure. need legal and incident comms. Jane (legal-jane) can you triage disclosure obligations?
legal-jane: on it. initial ask: we need exact count of affected customers, object identifiers (non-sensitive hashes ok), window, and whether any public crawling could have occurred. Also whether data content is accessible via presign or only metadata.
security-guy: running an access replay audit — checking logs for GET requests to presigned URLs.
ops-runner: statuspage-bot: Draft statuspage incident created: "Upload service — possible presign URL exposure" (investigating). Not yet posted.
alex.w: create internal incident channel for comms and attach checklists: PII exposure checklist, regulatory trigger matrix (GDPR/CCPA), timeline extraction, and customer notification draft.
statuspage-bot: added timeline placeholder and assigned incident severity: S2 (customer impact possible).
mira.k: update: we found 9 distinct GETs from outside our VPC to presigned URLs in the window. replay logs show 4 unique external IPs.
samir.p: extracting list of affected customer IDs (hashed) now. will publish counts only, not raw object keys, to legal.
legal-jane: please include the earliest and latest presign timestamps and the config change timestamp. We need to know if any presigns were long-lived. Also a note: if any EU customer data is implicated, we must notify DPO within 24h.
security-guy: replay audit finished — 9 GETs succeeded; content types indicate binary blobs (likely files). No obvious mass scanning. IPs look distributed; investigating if any known abuse lists.
alex.w: drafting customer notification — want a short, transparent email and a fuller technical appendix for customers who request details. I'll paste a working draft here; please comment.
alex.w: ```
Subject: Important: Potentially accessible file links in Uploads service

Hi —

We’re reaching out because our engineering team discovered a configuration issue that may have allowed presigned links to be issued for a short period, potentially making some files accessible to holders of those links. We’ve taken immediate steps to stop further issuance and are investigating the scope.

What we know so far:
- The issue occurred between 2026-03-14T15:02:12Z and 2026-03-14T15:14:10Z.
- We observed 9 external accesses to affected links; preliminary matching suggests up to ~36 customer-uploaded objects may be involved.
- We have revoked presigns and disabled the presign issuance while we remediate.

What we’re doing:
- Stopped presign issuance and rolled a fix.
- Conducting a full audit to identify impacted customers and objects.
- If we confirm your files were accessed, we will notify you with details and recommended steps.

What you can do:
- If you use presigned links, rotate any external shares created during the window.
- Contact support if you want assistance or an export of your affected objects.

We apologize for the inconvenience and are prioritizing a precise scope and follow-up.

— Redwood Inference Security
```
legal-jane: good start. tighten language around "may have allowed" -> must be clear about uncertainty. Add an explicit point on what data types we believe were in the files (e.g., logs, binaries) if known. Also add contact escalation: support-safety@redwood.ai, and include a subject line token for reference.
alex.w: edited draft inline, adding reference token and changing phrasing. pushing updated draft to thread.
alex.w: ```
Subject: [Redwood Incident #2026-1849997777] Potentially accessible file links — immediate notice

Hi —

We are notifying you that our team discovered a configuration issue that may have resulted in presigned URLs being issued for a short window, potentially allowing file access to holders of those links. At this time, we have limited evidence of external access, and investigations are ongoing.

What we know so far:
- Window: 2026-03-14T15:02:12Z to 2026-03-14T15:14:10Z.
- Observed external GETs: 9.
- Estimated affected customer objects: up to ~36 (subject to confirmation).
- Types: content appears to be user-uploaded assets (binary files); we have not verified presence of PII in those objects.

Actions we’ve taken:
- Disabled presign issuance and deployed a config fix.
- Revoked existing presigns where possible and are rotating short-lived keys.
- Performing a customer-by-customer audit; affected customers will receive targeted notifications if their objects were accessed.

If your files were accessed, we will provide: a timeline, object manifest (hashed identifiers), and recommended remediation steps.

Contact: support-safety@redwood.ai (please reference Incident #2026-1849997777).

We understand the seriousness of this issue and will update you as we confirm more details.

— Redwood Inference Security
```
ops-runner: heads up — statuspage requires a 280-char summary for the public post. alex.w can you create a short status blurb we can post in 30m if we need to?
alex.w: sure — draft: "Investigating a potential accidental issuance of presigned file links for a short window. No confirmed widespread access; targeted notifications will follow if we verify access."
legal-jane: for regulatory compliance, prepare a log export and a per-customer risk matrix. Also collect retention policy for each implicated customer if they're EU-based.
mira.k: working with infra to pull the presign issuance logs and the revocation actions, ETA 45m.
samir.p: I'll prepare the checklist for customer outreach: initial notice, detailed follow-up, remediation steps, potential compensation talk track.
security-guy: more: if we end up needing to notify regulators, we should prepare a timeline with exact timestamps and a post-incident remediation plan.
eng-lead: priority: accurate counts before any public post. do not post to statuspage or send mass emails until counts confirmed or legal okays preliminary notice.
statuspage-bot: draft saved as public update candidate 1. scheduled for review.
legal-jane: agreed — we can send targeted customer notices now for those we confirm, public statuspage only after legal sign-off on wording.
alex.w: action items summarized:
- mira.k: extract impacted object list and external GET details (ETA 45m).
- samir.p: assemble customer-contact mapping and outreach checklist (ETA 60m).
- security-guy: finish IP and access forensic (ETA 30m).
- ops-runner: prepare rollback options and revocation scripts.
- legal-jane: draft regulator notification template in case it’s required.
- alex.w: prepare customer and public messaging drafts and keep thread updated.

oncall-bot: Reminder: next oncall rotation in 2 hours. If this escalates, please handoff appropriately.
alex.w: thanks all. I'll update thread with confirmed counts. trying to keep messaging tight and avoid alarm until we know more. :handshake:
